# compose-hardware-insets

> An Android Compose library for hardware that is physically in the way of your UI: display cutouts
> and waterfall curves. Compose exposes how deep the cutout goes into each edge but not where the
> camera is, so there is no supported way to ask whether the hardware is in the way of one
> particular control. This answers that, and keeps the geometry pure so it can be tested against
> hardware you do not own.

Kotlin, Android, minSdk 23, Apache 2.0. Maven coordinates `io.github.damson:hardware-insets`.

## Public API

- `ScreenEdge`: `TOP`, `BOTTOM`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`. `TOP` and `BOTTOM` are edges of the screen and
  never move; `LEFT` and `RIGHT` are edges of the device held upright. `isHorizontalEdge`,
  `opposite`. Treat the constant names as a stored format if you persist one.
- `ScreenEdge.onScreenAt(rotation: ScreenRotation)`: which screen edge a device edge has become.
  Always returns a horizontal edge.
- `ScreenRotation`: `NONE`, `QUARTER`, `HALF`, `THREE_QUARTERS`. Named rather than an `Int`, because
  `Configuration.ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE` is 2 and so is `Surface.ROTATION_180`. Read one off a
  display with `Display.screenRotation`.
- `WindowCorner`: `TOP_LEFT`, `TOP_RIGHT`, `BOTTOM_LEFT`, `BOTTOM_RIGHT`. Which corner a control is
  tucked into.
- `BarBehavior`: `SHOW_TRANSIENT_ON_SWIPE`, `PLATFORM_DEFAULT`. What a hidden bar does when reached
  for.
- `CutoutShape(bounds: List<Rect>, topInset, bottomInset, leftInset, rightInset)`: `bounds` is where
  the cameras are, in pixels, in window coordinates. Empty below API 28 and on hardware with no
  cutout.
- `View.cutoutShape(): State<CutoutShape>`: live state, refreshed on every inset dispatch. Registers
  the view's single `OnApplyWindowInsetsListener`, so never call it on a `ComposeView`, whose
  `setContent` claims that slot silently.
- `View.stopReportingCutoutShape()`: removes it. Clears the whole slot, not just this listener.
- `HardwarePolicy(isCutoutIncluded = true, isWaterfallIncluded = true, areSystemBarsIncluded = false)`:
  which of the window's insets count as hardware.
- `hardwareInsets(position: ScreenEdge = TOP, policy: HardwarePolicy = HardwarePolicy(), isFarEdgeIgnored: Boolean = false): WindowInsets`
- `Modifier.clearOfTheHardware(...)`: the same, as padding. Apply after a background, so the
  background keeps its full size and only what is inside it moves.
- `cornerClearance(cutoutBounds: List<Rect>, position: ScreenEdge = TOP, isAtTheEnd: Boolean = false): (controlWidth: Int) -> IntOffset`:
  horizontal edges only; returns a function answering `IntOffset.Zero` on `LEFT` or `RIGHT`.
- `cornerClearanceFor(cutoutBounds, controlWidth, sideInset, windowSize, corner): IntOffset`:
  the pure geometry, public so a caller can ask it directly and test it.
- `CutoutMode`: `ALWAYS` (falls back to `SHORT_EDGES` below API 30), `SHORT_EDGES`, `DEFAULT`,
  `NEVER`.
- `ComponentActivity.drawBehindTheHardware(statusBarStyle: SystemBarStyle? = null, navigationBarStyle: SystemBarStyle? = null, cutoutMode: CutoutMode = ALWAYS)`:
  null styles keep whatever `enableEdgeToEdge` picks. `cutoutMode` is ignored below API 28.
- `ComponentActivity.hideTheSystemBars(types: Int = WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars(), behavior: BarBehavior = BarBehavior.SHOW_TRANSIENT_ON_SWIPE)`

## Traps a caller hits

- A centred punch-hole reports an inset across the whole window width. Padding by it moves a corner
  control far clear of a camera it never overlapped. That is what `cornerClearance` exists for.
- A `wrap_content` `ComposeView` swallows every touch inside its bounds, so padding it on the edge
  away from its content turns that padding into surface nobody can reach. `isFarEdgeIgnored = true`
  is the opt out, and it is off by default because it is a host's workaround rather than a fact
  about hardware.
- The system bars still report insets while hidden, which is why they are excluded by default.
- `waterfall` is always zero below API 30 and `displayCutout` below API 28. Neither needs a branch
  in your code.
